m1-freshness-kinda.title: Kind A: fix check_skill_freshness.py interpreter-guess mirror bug
m1-freshness-kinda.imperative: Root cause (confirmed by investigation): scripts/check_skill_freshness.py's _normalized_hash() reverses the installer's `python <` -> `<interpreter> <` rewrite by GUESSING the interpreter via a local os.name-based _platform_interpreter() mirror, instead of reading the actual per-skill interpreter.json sidecar install_constellation.py writes. On this POSIX host the real host probe resolves 'py' (order py/python3/python, all three resolve via the fixed pyfix-venv), but the freshness guess hardcodes 'python3' for os.name != 'nt' -- producing a false upstream-changed/project-customized read on an untouched template. Fix: add a helper that reads skills_root/<skill>/interpreter.json for the actual resolved interpreter, falling back to _platform_interpreter() only when the sidecar is absent; use it in _normalized_hash instead of the direct _platform_interpreter() call. This is shipped-code POSIX defect fixing (do NOT touch the three assertions in tests/test_feedback_tooling.py::FreshnessPathTokenTests or tests/test_install_constellation.py::TemplateBaselineTests -- they are correct). Do not change install_constellation.py's INTERPRETER_CANDIDATES order.

postconditions.statement: the three Kind-A tests pass: FreshnessPathTokenTests (both) + TemplateBaselineTests::test_seeded_working_copy_reads_up_to_date_against_baseline

constraints: do not change interpreter candidate order

m2-interp-probe-kindb.title: Kind B: platform-aware InterpreterProbeTests sidecar test
m2-interp-probe-kindb.imperative: tests/test_install_constellation.py::InterpreterProbeTests::test_sidecar_records_resolved_via_for_probe_success_and_fallback fails on Linux with NotImplementedError: cannot instantiate 'WindowsPath' -- because the fallback half of the test wraps the FULL install_skills() call (which internally calls write_corpus_marker -> compute_corpus_id, which does a bare Path(skills_dir) re-wrap) inside mock.patch.object(installer.os, 'name', 'nt'). Path()'s class-selection reads os.name at call time, so the re-wrap silently becomes a WindowsPath instance; the next path-join on it invokes WindowsPath.__new__ directly, which raises for real on a POSIX host. This exact hazard is ALREADY documented 20 lines above in the same file (_install_commander_spine's comment: 'os.name can't be safely faked around a full install because pathlib refuses to build a foreign path flavor'). Fix by following that established local convention: narrow the os.name mock to wrap ONLY the resolve_interpreter() call (matching test_resolve_interpreter_falls_back_to_os_default_on_total_failure's pattern), then pass the resulting InterpreterResolution explicitly via install_skills(..., interpreter=resolution) so install_skills does not re-probe and the corpus-marker path never runs under spoofed os.name. Keep asserting the same Windows-fallback semantics (resolved_via=='os-default-fallback', interpreter=='py') -- do not weaken to something platform-generic.
constraints: do not change interpreter candidate order

m3-normcase-kindb.title: Kind B: platform-gate test_same_path_windows_normcase_sep_equivalence
m3-normcase-kindb.imperative: tests/test_spine_rail.py::test_same_path_windows_normcase_sep_equivalence asserts sr._same_path('C:\\Foo','c:/foo') is True, relying on ntpath's normcase (lowercases + folds backslash/forward-slash). On POSIX, os.path.normcase is identity and backslash is not a separator, so posixpath correctly treats these as two DIFFERENT strings -- the shipped _same_path (scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py:313, wraps os.path.normcase+normpath) is doing the platform-correct thing on both platforms; the test just hardcodes Windows-only folding as if it were universal. Fix: skip the Windows assertion on non-Windows via pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform != 'win32', reason=...) (sys already imported in this file), and ADD a companion test asserting the platform-correct POSIX behaviour (is False, i.e. no spurious relaxation on POSIX either) skipped on win32. Do not delete the Windows test or weaken its assertion -- it must keep asserting True under skipif so Windows behaviour is still proven when the suite runs there.

postconditions.statement: same_path tests pass on this POSIX host, Windows assertion preserved under skipif

m4-hang-cmd-kindb.title: Kind B: POSIX-native hang primitive for test_real_runner_process_death
m4-hang-cmd-kindb.imperative: tests/test_run_skill_eval.py::test_real_runner_process_death_leaves_resumable_state fails with PermissionError on hang.cmd: _write_hang_cmd() (tests/test_run_skill_eval.py ~line 1253) always writes a Windows .cmd batch file and spawns it via Popen(shell=False), which cannot execute on Linux (no exec bit, no shebang, not a PE). The production code under test, run_skill_eval._tree_kill (scripts/run_skill_eval.py:621), is ALREADY portable -- it branches on os.name and falls back to proc.kill() on non-Windows (comment: 'kept so the module is portable'), so no change is needed there. Fix _write_hang_cmd to branch on os.name: keep the existing .cmd/py-c shim on Windows verbatim, and on POSIX write a shebang'd shell script (#!/bin/sh invoking sys.executable -c 'import time; time.sleep(600)'), chmod it executable (os.chmod, no new import needed), and return that path instead. Generalize _confirm_hang_primitive's docstring/messages away from the literal '.cmd' where they'd now be inaccurate on POSIX, without changing its behavior (still fail loudly, never silently switch mechanisms mid-test). Do not touch run_skill_eval.py's _tree_kill or any other shipped code -- this is a test-fixture-only fix.

postconditions.statement: the real-process-death test passes on POSIX via a real killed subprocess
